verdicts.gap_description: C0005 is stated only as a finite verification, so the universal premise N(r)=q_n+1 is not proved in the text; it is fillable in two lines from the recurrence (f(q_n,r_n)=q_n forces f(q,r_n)=q_n for all q>=q_n via the elif clause, so the last genuine P-position is exactly q_n), but this requires the cited BHMS constant-row property f(q_n,r_n)=q_n and the identification of stale rows with constant rows, neither proved here. Separately, the sole load-bearing inequality q_n <= 3n-1 is outsourced entirely to BHMS 8.8, which I could not check (no network in the sandbox); it is numerically corroborated to n = 58579.

verdicts.first_gap_line: "N(r_n)  =  q_n + 1                          (ingredient 3)"  /  "**N(r) = q_n + 1 for a stale row** (claim C0005, verified for all 29289 stale rows to r = 50000)"
verdicts.gap_description: Ingredient 3 (N(r_n) = q_n + 1) is the first step not established by proof: it needs the fact that a stale row's constant value is attained exactly at q = the value, i.e. that the mex branch of the recurrence can never kill a row at a value strictly below the diagonal (otherwise the last genuine P-position sits above q_n and N > q_n + 1). The text supplies only numerical verification for this (its own C0005 is labelled 'evidence not proof'); the parenthetical 'the start of the constant row' assumes precisely what needs showing. The gap is fillable — either from BHMS's constant-row structure or by a short recurrence argument (before the freeze point f(q,r) >= q+1 with pairwise distinct values, and the freeze value is f(q0,r) at the first q0 with f(q0,r) <= q0; one must exclude f(q0,r) < q0). Secondary caveat: BHMS 8.8's q_n <= 3n-1 could not be checked against the source text in this sandbox (network access refused); the citation is numerically consistent and the submission's characterization of q_n (n-th integer not on the diagonal {f(m,m)}) was independently confirmed against the solver.

verdicts.effectivity_check: Effectivity is fine: the bound is explicit and computable, K(r) = 3r, produced at the line "N(r_n)  =  q_n + 1 ... <= (3n - 1) + 1 = 3n ... <= 3 r_n" with ingredient 2 "r_n >= n for all n >= 1". No dependence on Byrnes' non-effective eventual periodicity and no constant asserted to exist without being computed. Caveat: the chain's input q_n <= 3n-1 is cited from print (BHMS 8.8) rather than re-derived; conditional on that citation, evaluating K(1000) = 3000 is immediate. The submission does not touch live rows (41422 of 100000 checked), so it closes only the stale-row sub-goal (B1), not the full N(r) target.
